en: From the Catalogue of Newly Imported Scriptures and Other Items in the Imperial Collection: A Table of the Catalogue of Newly Imported Scriptures and Other Items.
Statement by the Śramaṇa Kūkai, who traveled to Tang China to study the Dharma: Kūkai departed in the twentieth year of the Enryaku era.
After three years,
at the conclusion of my mission to study abroad,
I sought the way across ten thousand li.
In the twelfth month of that year, he arrived in Chang’an.
On the tenth day of the second month of the twenty-fourth year,
by imperial decree, he was assigned to reside at Ximing Monastery.
Thereupon, he traveled extensively among various temples,
seeking out and selecting a master upon whom to rely.
Fortunately, he encountered the Abbot Hui-guo, a Dharma-named *ācārya* of consecration at Qinglong Temple.
He was taken as his master.
As for his great virtue, he was a Dharma-transmitting disciple of the Tripitaka Master Amoghavajra of Da Xingshan Temple,
who had mastered the sutras and vinaya and thoroughly penetrated the esoteric treasury.
The fundamental principles of the Dharma are the teachers of the state;
may the Great Master further the dissemination of the Buddha-Dharma.
He sighed over the people of this world who could be liberated,
bestowed upon me the precepts for generating the bodhicitta,
and granted me permission to enter the mandala of empowerment.
He received the clear consecration (vidyābhiṣeka) two or three times,
and was invested with the rank of ācārya once.
He practiced both the learned and the unlearned through crawling on his elbows and walking on his knees.
I prostrate at his feet and listen to what has been heard and not yet heard.
By the great grace of the State and the compassion of the Great Master,
I have studied the Great Dharma of the two divisions.
To practice the yoga of the various Honored Ones—
this dharma is the very heart-essence of all Buddhas and the path to attaining Buddhahood.
In the city walls of the kingdom, there is human fat and marrow;
therefore, those of meager fortune do not hear its name,
and heavy defilements cannot enter it.
In India, the Tripiṭaka Master Śubhakarasiṃha cast off his sandals and ascended the throne; in China, Emperor Xuanzong looked up to it with such reverence that he forgot the taste of food.
From that time until now, successive sovereigns and high ministers have followed one another’s footsteps in their devotion to its study.
The fourfold assembly and the myriad people bowed their heads and opened their treasure chests;
from this point on, the school of the Secret Treasury was proclaimed Emperor,
while the manifest teachings of the Half-Bead were defeated, their banners lowered and their leaders bound.
For when the phoenix flies, it must seek out the reigns of Yao and Shun; so too,
the practice and concealment of the Buddha-dharma unfold and contract according to the times.
Now, more than one hundred sections of the Vajrayāna teachings have been invited and brought here,
as seen in the oceanic assembly of the two great maṇḍalas;
though it is said that the waves were vast and turbulent, and the ship was tossed by wind and rain.
To cross that whale-ocean and reach the realm of the sages is made possible solely by the power of the sages.
We humbly submit that Your Majesty, the Emperor, possesses a supreme virtue as vast as heaven.
The Buddha-sun rises ever higher;
the Buddha is the father of mankind.
Moved by compassion for the common people, he wets his feet with their suffering.
Zhongfo entrusted the succession and passed on the mantle of governance;
as Your Majesty has newly ascended the celestial pivot,
newly translated scriptures have arrived from afar.
Since Your Majesty has nurtured all within the four seas with compassion,
the arrival of this image from across the sea is as if it were a perfect tally.
Were it not for the Noble Ones, who could fathom this?
Although Kūkai may have committed the sin of failing to meet his appointed time, he feels that death would be more than sufficient;
yet he privately rejoices that he was born to request and bring back this dharma so difficult to encounter.
Unable to bear the arrival of either extreme fear or joy,
I respectfully entrust this memorial to the Great Minister, the Great Overseer of the High Rank, the Real Man Yuancheng, who serves as the Official of the Sixth Rank,
Upper Division, to present for imperial perusal.
I have also requested a one-volume catalog of newly translated scriptures and other texts, which I now respectfully present to Your Majesty;
I am deeply apprehensive at having thus intruded upon Your august presence.
I remain prostrate in trepidation.
I, the śramaṇa Kūkai, with utmost trepidation and reverence, respectfully submit this memorial.

On the twenty-second day of the tenth month of the first year of the Daitō era, the śramaṇa Kūkai, who has entered Tang China to study the Dharma, presents this petition. and so forth; the Samaya-maṇḍala and the Dharma-maṇḍala.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Amoghavajra, who held the rank of Special Advance (Tèjìn), served as Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial (Hónglùqīng), was additionally invested with the title of Peer of the State (Kāifǔ Yítóng sānsī),
was enfeoffed as Duke of Sù, was posthumously honored as Minister of Works (Sīkōng), and was bestowed the posthumous title Dàbiànzhèng Dàguǎngzhì.
The single flavor of the Dharma-ocean accords with the depth or shallowness of individual capacities;
the five vehicles diverge according to their vessels, whether sudden or gradual.
Within the Sudden Teaching, there is both the manifest and the esoteric.
Regarding the Secret Treasury, there are both its source and its branches.
The Dharma masters of old swam the branches and climbed the trees;
what is transmitted today uproots the weeds and exhausts the source.
Why is this? In the past, Vajrasattva personally received it from the Tathāgata Samantaprabhāsa;
several hundred years later, he transmitted it to the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna.
Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna transmitted it to Ācārya Nāgabodhi;
Ācārya Nāgabodhi transmitted it to Ācārya Vajrabodhi.
During the Kaiyuan era of the Great Tang, the Tripiṭaka Master Vajrabodhi first introduced the five families [of esoteric Buddhism].
Although it was said that one person revered and upheld it,
it could not be widely disseminated;
only our ancestor, the Great Ācārya of Vast Wisdom (Mahāprajñā), [was able to do so].
Having first received the Vajrajñāna Tripiṭaka,
he further traveled to the master Nāgabodhi in South India,
where he mastered the eighteen assemblies of the Yoga Tantra.
He thoroughly investigated the secret treasuries, such as the *Tāizàng* (Womb Realm) Maṇḍala.
During the Tiānbǎo era, he returned to the Great Táng.
At that time, Emperor Xuānzōng first received the consecration (*abhiṣeka*).
He humbled himself to serve as a master and disciple,
personally receiving the Dharma from Emperor Suzong and Emperor Daizong in succession.
Within the imperial palace, he established the Shenlong Vihāra.
Within the city, the empowerment mandala was opened everywhere;
one person and the hundred officials attended the mandala to receive empowerment,
while the fourfold assembly and the multitudes of living beings knelt and crawled to study the Secret Treasury.
The school of the Secret Treasury flourished like the rising sun;
the dharma of consecration (abhiṣeka) has followed in its wake from this point onward.
Furthermore, while the Exoteric Teachings discourse upon the distant kalpas of the Three Greats, [the Esoteric Teachings speak of the three mysteries].
The Secret Treasury (Guhyagarbha) anticipates the great birth at the age of sixteen;
its variations in speed and excellence are like those of a supernatural power versus a lame donkey.
May guests who look up to the virtuous understand this intent.

The relative superiority and inferiority of the teachings and the origins of their various systems are explained in detail in such works as the *Vajrasattva-pañca-guhya-vidhi* and the correspondence between the Great Dharma Master Bianzheng and the Tripiṭaka Master [Xuanzang].
